# Neon Pulsar: Zero-G Arena — project facts

## Identity and attribution

- Title: Neon Pulsar: Zero-G Arena
- Author and lead creator: Aarti S Ravikumar (Aarti Sri Ravikumar), https://ai-aarti.com/
- Engineering team credited by the project: PCSS II Robotics Team, https://pcssiirobotics.org/
- Source code and detailed documentation: https://github.com/aartisr/hackclub-neon-pulsar
- Public project and creator credits: /about.html

## What the game does

Neon Pulsar is a browser-based multiplayer disc game set in a 3D zero-gravity arena. One player hosts a room and shares a code or invite link. Others join the room and choose Team Cyan or Team Magenta. Players fly into the white disc to pick it up and throw it toward the opposing team's colored goal. First to five points wins.

On a keyboard, WASD moves, Space rises, Shift descends, and E throws while carrying the disc. T opens chat with everyone and Y opens team chat. The game menu lets a player switch sides or leave. A host leaving closes the room for everyone; a guest leaving disconnects only that guest.

## Implementation

- React and TypeScript provide the interface.
- Three.js renders the 3D arena.
- PeerJS uses WebRTC data connections for multiplayer. A signaling service establishes connections; the host runs the authoritative simulation and sends state updates.
- Match replays and browser-generated audio are included.
- Career statistics are stored locally in the browser. The landing-page standings are sample data, not a live global leaderboard.

These facts reflect the public repository. For current implementation details and limitations, inspect the source code and README. Do not describe the game as having zero latency or a persistent global leaderboard.
